description: We are Team WUNDERBAO, interested in space science, microgravity combustion, and spacecraft fire safety. FLARE combines a D² Law simulator, 3D chamber, NASA research, scenario comparisons, an AI science assistant, and kid-friendly learning. Join us to make complex science accessible and learn together. We welcome skills in physics, React/TypeScript, 3D/WebGL, UI/UX, NASA data, AI, or storytelling and presentations.
summary:
FLARE (Fire & Life-Safety Analysis and Risk Explorer) is an interactive platform for exploring combustion and fire safety in microgravity. It combines an adjustable D² Law analytical simulator with a 3D chamber, live visual readouts, and controls for gravity, oxygen, pressure, airflow, and fuel. Users can explore 16 NASA combustion investigations, compare research cases with model scenarios, and learn through a kid-friendly flame sandbox and AI science assistant.

FLARE addresses the challenge by making it easier to investigate how reduced buoyancy changes flame shape and how cabin conditions affect combustion. This is important because understanding fire behavior supports safer spacecraft design, fire detection, and crew protection on long-duration missions. Simulation results are analytical model estimates, not raw spacecraft measurements or full CFD predictions.
details:
FLARE (Fire & Life-Safety Analysis and Risk Explorer) is an interactive web platform for exploring how combustion changes in microgravity and why spacecraft fire safety matters. In the scientific workspace, users adjust fuel, sample size, gravity, oxygen concentration, pressure, and airflow. A simplified D² Law analytical model estimates combustion behavior and displays results in an interactive 3D chamber with diagnostic layers and telemetry. Users can also explore 16 curated NASA combustion investigations and compare research cases with model scenarios.

FLARE makes complex space-combustion concepts easier to investigate for students, educators, researchers, and the public. Its intended impact is to build understanding of how cabin conditions affect fire behavior and crew safety, while clearly distinguishing model estimates from measured data. The separate FLARE Kids experience introduces the same ideas through an interactive flame sandbox, guided learning worlds, and Sparky, a child-friendly science assistant.

We developed FLARE with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Three.js, and React Three Fiber. NASA Physical Sciences Informatics and NASA Technical Reports Server records inform the research experience; Gemini can power the AI assistant, which also has a demo mode.

Our creative approach combines a research instrument, NASA investigation explorer, scenario comparison tools, and a kid-friendly learning space in one platform. We considered scientific transparency, source attribution, accessibility, reduced motion, responsive layouts, and safe explanations for young learners. FLARE is an educational analytical tool, not a full CFD solver or a source of raw spacecraft telemetry.
